AnimatedCounter.summary: Number counting from `from` to `to` over durationMs; startMs, hitAt, ease, steps, ticks and stepsAt shape it.
AnimatedCounter.doc: Counts from `from` to `to` over `durationMs` (from `startMs`, shaped by `ease`, in `steps` jumps when set), as a pure function of the timeline; inside an `AnimatedGroup` the group's alpha multiplies into the fill and shine-capable groups mount the band material so the sweep doesn't skip the digits, both structurally absent outside groups (standing bytes stay safe). With a `textKey` it joins the managed-text lifecycle, so it stands down under a generic takeover like every scene-owned text primitive.

props.name: durationMs
props.doc: Count-up duration, in ms (local scene time); `steps` jumps inside it, `stepsAt` replaces it.

props.name: format
props.doc: Formats the interpolated value for display. Defaults to a rounded integer.

props.name: anchorX
props.doc: Where `position` sits on the number's X axis (default "center", the legacy contract).

props.name: textKey
props.doc: The sidecar style key this counter honours: registers the row in the Edit-text drill and applies the `textStyle.<textKey>*` overrides (Size/Color/Font/OffsetX/OffsetY/RotationDeg).

props.name: startMs
props.doc: When the count starts, in ms (scene-local; default 0).

props.name: hitAt
props.doc: Scene-local ms the count LANDS on `to`, on a beat or a cut: it starts `durationMs` earlier. Wins over `startMs`; `stepsAt` ignores it.

props.name: ease
props.doc: An ease name shaping the count (default "linear"). With `steps` it moves when each jump falls; with `stepsAt` or `ticks` it bends how far each jump goes.

props.name: steps
props.doc: Count in this many equal jumps instead of continuously, landing on `to`: a jump falls where the eased progress crosses each k/n, so the first comes after 1/n of the count (never at `startMs`), the last exactly at the end, and `ease` shifts the ones between.

props.name: ticks
props.doc: "beats": one jump on every grid beat from the start of the count to its end, each with a pop, landing on `to` on the last. Counts continuously (with one log line) when the project has no grid.

props.name: stepsAt
props.doc: One jump (with a pop) at each scene-local ms, landing on `to` on the last. Wins over `ticks`, `steps` and the count window.

props.name: pop
props.doc: The scale each `ticks` or `stepsAt` jump pops by (default 0.08, so 1.08 and back over 180 ms); 0 turns it off.

props.name: anchorY
props.doc: Where `position` sits on the number's Y axis (default "middle").

timing: The count runs startMs to startMs + durationMs. hitAt lands it on `to` at that ms, starting durationMs earlier.
steps: equal jumps where the EASED progress crosses each k/n, so the first falls after 1/n (never at startMs), the last exactly at the end, and ease moves the ones between.

stepsAt: one jump at each ms, whatever the window says, landing on `to` on the last. ticks="beats": one on every grid beat inside the window. Both pop; with them ease bends how far each jump goes, not when.

AnimatedGroup.summary: Animates icon + text lockups as one unit with the text presets.
AnimatedGroup.doc: Animates its children as one unit through the shared text-preset sampler, the group mechanism for icon+text lockups: granularity is forced null (`scatter-scale` on a group is the whole-lockup degenerate), child presets compose (alphas multiply through `GroupAnimationContext`, transforms nest), and the pivot is deliberately the group's origin since measured-bounds pivots depend on load timing, a determinism smell.

props.name: from
props.doc: In-animation start, in ms (local scene time).

props.name: to
props.doc: In-animation end, in ms.

props.name: hitAt
props.doc: Scene-local ms the group LANDS (first at rest size and full opacity), on a beat or a cut: the in keeps its duration and starts the motion's measured lead earlier. Wins over `from`.

props.name: outAt
props.doc: Out start, in ms; the out plays over the same duration as the in.

props.name: durationMs
props.doc: Pins the reveal (the group is one unit) to this many ms; "authored" or absent keeps the authored window.

props.name: preset
props.doc: In-animation preset. Defaults to the theme's `textAnimation.in`.

props.name: outPreset
props.doc: Out-animation preset; plays only when `outAt` is set.

props.name: ease
props.doc: Easing for preset animations. Defaults to the theme's `motion.easings.standard`.

props.name: startScale
props.doc: fade-scale: starting scale, landing at 1.

props.name: shine
props.doc: fade-scale and twist-scale: sweep the soft white shine band once across the whole lockup.

props.name: direction
props.doc: twist-scale: the side the card turns in from.

props.name: em
props.doc: World units per em for offset presets (default 0.6).

props.name: extent
props.doc: Group extent [width, height] the shine band sweeps, group-local units.

props.name: textKey
props.doc: Stable managed-text key used to resolve an item-level motion exception.

props.name: ignoreSceneMotion
props.doc: Keep this coded group reveal independent of the scene motion fields.

props.name: imageEffects
props.doc: Lets managed image icons participate in blur-in and mask-reveal.

timing: from to to is the in window, the whole group one unit. durationMs pins it; hitAt lands it, starting the motion's lead earlier and winning over `from`.
An out starts at outAt and plays over the same duration as the in.

AnimatedHeadline.summary: The core SDF text primitive: presets, stagger, looks, depth, fit, hitAt, opacity, textKey styling.
AnimatedHeadline.doc: SDF headline rendered through troika (via drei `<Text>`); all motion is a pure function of the timeline, never the wall clock. Three render paths chosen once per mount: LEGACY (nothing configured, the original v0 linear fillOpacity ramp byte-for-byte, must not change), BLOCK (preset without stagger, whole-block opacity/offset/blur/clip via troika props), and STAGGERED (staggerMs > 0, one mesh with a per-glyph derived material).

props.name: from
props.doc: Reveal start, in ms (local scene time).

props.name: to
props.doc: Reveal end, in ms (local scene time).

props.name: preset
props.doc: In-animation preset. Defaults to the theme's `textAnimation.in`.

props.name: outPreset
props.doc: Out-animation preset; plays only when `outAt` is set. Defaults to `textAnimation.out`.

props.name: outAt
props.doc: Out start, in ms; the out plays over the same duration as the in unless `outDurationMs` sets its own.

props.name: outDurationMs
props.doc: How long the out lasts, ms (default the in's duration).

props.name: hitAt
props.doc: Scene-local ms the first unit LANDS (first at rest size and full opacity), on a beat or a cut: the in keeps its duration and starts the motion's measured lead earlier, `delayMs` included. Wins over `from`; the out never moves.

props.name: opacity
props.doc: 0..1, multiplied into every fade (default 1).

props.name: stagger
props.doc: Per-char / per-word stagger granularity. Paragraph delivery is spelled through `delivery`, never here.

props.name: staggerMs
props.doc: Per-unit stagger delay, ms. Defaults to the theme's `textAnimation.staggerMs`.

props.name: delayMs
props.doc: Hold before the in starts, ms (clamped ≥ 0; the out never shifts). Defaults to `textAnimation.delayMs`.

props.name: durationMs
props.doc: Pins the whole reveal, first unit's start to last unit's settle, to this many ms for the text's unit count (stagger and unit duration scale together); "authored" or absent keeps the authored per-unit timing.

props.name: startScale
props.doc: fade-scale: starting scale, landing at 1 (default 0.8, clamped 0.05-4).

props.name: shine
props.doc: fade-scale: sweep the soft white shine band once during the scale-in.

props.name: direction
props.doc: twist-scale: the side the card turns in from (default "from-left").

props.name: buildShiftEm
props.doc: build: how far each arriving word slides in, em (default 0.3).

props.name: delivery
props.doc: all-at-once / by-paragraph / by-paragraph-group. Paragraphs split on `\n`, groups on blank lines; all-at-once forces the whole-block path.

props.name: ease
props.doc: Easing for preset animations. Defaults to the theme's `motion.easings.standard`.

props.name: face
props.doc: Which theme face renders the text: the headline or body font.

props.name: color
props.doc: Theme colour token filling the text, or a raw sRGB hex (the per-scene text-colour escape hatch; tokens stay the default). Setting this pins the fill: the sidecar can no longer override it and the Edit-text drill-in shows no swatch. Prefer `defaultColor` on sidecar-driven scenes.

props.name: textKey
props.doc: The sidecar text key this headline renders (what `useSceneText` was called with): enables the app-editable fill (`textStyle.<textKey>Color` in the scene document) and registers the field's colour swatch in the inspector.

props.name: styleKey
props.doc: Compatibility-only style source when the stable managed key differs from an older sidecar style key.

props.name: motionKey
props.doc: Compatibility-only motion source when the stable managed key differs from an older keyed override.

props.name: defaultColor
props.doc: Fill when neither `color` nor the sidecar set one (default "text"): the token a scene wants as its design default while staying app-editable.

props.name: fontRef
props.doc: Explicit font override replacing the theme face; also how the dispatcher applies a sidecar `<textKey>Font`.

props.name: textAlign
props.doc: Per-line alignment inside the measured block (visible on multi-line text only).

props.name: anchorX
props.doc: Where `position` sits on the block's X axis (default "center", the legacy contract).

props.name: anchorY
props.doc: Where `position` sits on the block's Y axis (default troika "middle"); "top" anchors multi-line blocks by their top edge so following content can budget below them.

props.name: maxWidth
props.doc: Wrap width in world units; unset means no wrapping, `\n` is the only line break. With `fit` it is the width to fit instead, and nothing wraps.

props.name: fit
props.doc: "width" shrinks the font (never grows it) so the widest line fits `maxWidth`, or the safe width when that's unset.

props.name: depth
props.doc: A layered depth look in any checked font: a stack of the same text receding behind the face, shading dark to light. `true` takes the finished default.

props.name: lineHeight
props.doc: Line spacing as a multiple of the font size; unset means troika's own "normal" (the font's metrics), which is also how the dispatcher applies a sidecar `<textKey>LineHeight`.

props.name: managedTextRole
props.doc: Scene text stands down when `managedText` is present. Embedded composition text opts out; managed renderer nodes opt back in.

props.name: managedTextCodedMotion
props.doc: Effective coded parent motion to retain if the inspector takes ownership of this line.

props.name: look
props.doc: Text-look preset name (the style catalogue); resolution follows the textAnimation pattern (theme default → sidecar `textLook` → props, `textLookForce` flips the order).

props.name: lookParams
props.doc: Look parameter overrides riding beside `look` (colours, angle, stroke, intensity, offset, curve).

AnimatedHeadline.example: <AnimatedHeadline text={title} textKey="title" fontSize={0.6} preset="stamp" hitAt={grid?.bar(5) ?? 2000} to={600} />
timing: from to to is the in window, ms: each unit plays the whole window and later units start stagger ms later, so the last settles after `to`.
A motion's durationMs wins over `to`: the `durationMs` prop pins first unit's start to last unit's settle (stagger and unit duration scale together), a sidecar spec's durationMs replaces the window.

hitAt is the first unit's landing: the in keeps its duration and starts the motion's lead earlier (delayMs included). See kb catalog textMotion for each motion's measured impactMs at 600 ms; it wins over `from`.
An out starts at outAt, plays over outDurationMs (default the in's duration) and never shifts with hitAt or delayMs.

ChartReveal.signature: interface ChartReveal { grow: number; alpha: number; count: number; pulse: number; shine: number; drop: number; }
ChartReveal.doc: Per-element build state. `grow` scales a mark from its base (0 = nothing there, 1 = final size; an overshoot preset may push it to `CHART_GROW_MAX` and a landing squash a little under 1). `alpha` multiplies its opacity. `count` is the CLAMPED, monotone counting channel a value label prints against (`value * count`), so a label never runs past the true value while `grow` overshoots. `pulse` is a 0..1 emphasis envelope (glow and scale pops), 0 at rest. `shine` is the shine-band sweep position, 0..1 with 1 = swept past; -1 = no band. `drop` translates the whole element along the VALUE axis in plot-space units (positive = displaced toward the far end), which is the one entrance a scaling channel cannot express; 0 at rest.

ChartRevealFn.doc: Per-element reveal lookup, called once per mark. Pie slices key on `categoryIndex`, line and area points on both. Absent means everything is fully revealed.

props.name: seed

props.doc: Glow: a target luminance (above a bloom threshold over 1) reached by raising only the tone's full channels, unlit with tone mapping off so it still lands exactly on the token (see `glowColour`). Absent renders as before.

props.doc: Theme colour token.

SceneTime.doc: Time exposed to a scene, all derived purely from the global clock.

ScreenFillProps.signature: interface ScreenFillProps { opacity?: number; keys?: readonly MotionKey[]; }
ScreenFillProps.doc: What every fill shares: an opacity and keys over any of its numbers (`tMs` is scene-local).

ScreenLayer.summary: Camera-locked layer in frame units with no depth test: order="front" over the finished frame, "back" behind everything 3D.
ScreenLayer.doc: A camera-locked layer laid out in frame units: (0, 0) is the centre and `useFormat().frame` the full size, whatever the scene camera does, and nothing in the 3D pass can hide it (no depth test). Replaces a hand-built pose in front of `useSceneCamera()`. For flat primitives (text, images, shapes, `Vignette`, `Scrim`, `Gradient`): a 3D model needs its depth test, and its materials are shared with any world copy. Both orders draw inside the compositor's own passes, so preview, Present and export agree.

props.name: order
props.doc: "front" (default) draws over the finished frame, past depth of field; "back" draws over the background and under everything 3D, and its pixels go through the scene's effects and transitions like the backdrop.

timing: Children stack in JSX order. front draws over the finished frame, past depth of field and, on a solo frame, past the effects; during a transition it crossfades with its scene and picks up the effects.
back draws over the background and under everything 3D, inside the scene's own pass: effects and depth of field apply to it like the backdrop.

Scrim.summary: Clear to a colour, linear or radial, for text to sit on; inside a ScreenLayer.
Scrim.doc: Clear to a colour, linear or radial, for text to sit on. Mount inside a `ScreenLayer`.

props.name: to
props.doc: The colour it deepens to: a theme token or hex (default "background").

props.name: kind
props.doc: "linear" (default) deepens along `angleDeg`; "radial" deepens from `centre` outward.

props.name: angleDeg
props.doc: Direction it deepens, degrees clockwise from up (default 180, solid at the bottom).

props.name: centre
props.doc: Radial centre, frame fractions from the bottom left (default [0.5, 0.5]).

props.name: start
props.doc: Where along the run it starts to show, 0..1 (default 0).

props.name: end
props.doc: Where along the run it goes solid, 0..1 (default 1).

props.name: opacity
props.doc: 0..1 (default 1).

props.name: keys
props.doc: Keyframes over `opacity` and the fill's numeric props; a key's `ease` shapes the segment arriving at it.

timing: keys override the props they name; a keyed fill holds stills until its last key lands.

ScrimProps.signature: interface ScrimProps extends ScreenFillProps { to?: Colour; kind?: "linear" | "radial"; angleDeg?: number; centre?: readonly [number, number]; start?: number; end?: number; }

SeededRandom.doc: A generator of floats in [0, 1), advancing on each call.

SharedKeyframe.signature: interface SharedKeyframe { tMs: number; position?: [number, number, number]; rotation?: [number, number, number]; scale?: number; opacity?: number; }
SharedKeyframe.doc: One morph keyframe. Fields are per-property optional (see engine/keyframes.ts).

SharedTransform.signature: interface SharedTransform { position: [number, number, number]; rotation: [number, number, number]; scale: number; opacity: number; }
SharedTransform.doc: A fully-resolved morph transform for one frame.

SplitField.summary: Frame split into tiles (images, videos, theme colours) with a staggered reveal that reflows per aspect; no tiles draws the sidecar mosaic.
SplitField.doc: A frame split into tiles (project images, videos or theme colours) with a staggered reveal; the grid reflows per aspect unless `columns` fixes it. Without `tiles` it draws the sidecar `mosaic` block, and mounting it stands the host fallback down.

props.name: tiles
props.doc: The tiles, in reading order; absent draws the sidecar `mosaic` block.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Fixed column count; absent picks the most square grid for the aspect, so the field reflows.

props.name: gap
props.doc: Gap between tiles as a fraction of the field's short side (default 0.02).

props.name: width
props.default: the whole frame at the field's depth
props.doc: Field size in world units (default the whole frame at the field's depth).

props.name: position
props.doc: Default [0, 0, -0.05], just behind content at z = 0.

SplitFieldProps.signature: interface SplitFieldProps { tiles?: SplitFieldTile[]; columns?: number; gap?: number; reveal?: SceneDocMosaicReveal; width?: number; height?: number; position?: V3; }

StagedObject.doc: One staged library object, from a sidecar `spec` or an `objectId` placed in TSX. `readObjectAsset` suspends until the manifest + URLs land (unknown ids degrade to nothing), then `LoadedObject` suspends on the glb through the objects' own gltf cache (both pre-warmed by the export preamble and the option-preview capture).

props.name: objectId
props.doc: A bundled id or `ws:<slug>`, as in `kb catalog objects`; an unknown id renders nothing.

props.name: position
props.doc: World position (default the origin).

props.name: rotationDeg
props.doc: Euler rotation, degrees (default none).

props.name: scale
props.doc: Multiplies the object's fitted size (default 1).

props.name: ground
props.doc: Sit the object on the stage floor; its y is then ignored (default false).

timing: objectId placed in TSX loads when it first mounts, even mid-film: every capture waits for it, so no frame shows it missing. A preview pops it in. No gizmo: use the sidecar `objects` array for an object the inspector should move.

StaggerGranularity.doc: Stagger granularities: words split on whitespace, chars are non-whitespace characters; paragraph granularities (spelled through `delivery`, never the public `stagger` prop) split on `\n` / blank lines and walk Y-key unit boundaries.

Stamp.summary: <Stamp at|hitAt rotateDeg? position rotation scale>: stamps children in at `at` ms (or landing on `hitAt`) with the stampScale pop and an optional rotation settle.
Stamp.doc: Stamps its children in at `at`: the `stampScale` pop (its defaults are contract) about the group origin, with an optional small rotation settle.

props.name: at
props.doc: Scene-local ms the stamp starts (default 0); hidden (at `from` scale) before it.

props.name: hitAt
props.doc: Scene-local ms the stamp LANDS (first reaches full size), on a beat or a cut; the stamp starts its measured lead earlier. Wins over `at`.

props.name: rotateDeg
props.doc: Optional settle: starts this many degrees off (about Z) and swings back to 0 with a small overshoot over the stamp.

props.name: rotation
props.doc: Radians; the settle adds to Z.

props.name: scale
props.doc: Base scale the stamp multiplies.

props.name: from
props.doc: Scale before the stamp starts.

props.name: peak
props.doc: Overshoot scale reached at `inMs`.

props.name: inMs
props.doc: `from` to `peak`, outCubic.

props.name: settleMs
props.doc: `peak` back to 1, inOutSine.

timing: at is when the pop starts; hitAt is when it first reaches full size, about 95 ms after the start on the default pop (kb catalog stamps). It overshoots at inMs and settles by inMs + settleMs.

StampProps.signature: interface StampProps extends StampScaleOptions { at?: number; hitAt?: number; rotateDeg?: number; position?: V3; rotation?: V3; scale?: number; children?: ReactNode; }

StampScaleOptions.signature: interface StampScaleOptions { from?: number; peak?: number; inMs?: number; settleMs?: number; }

TEXT_PRESET_NAMES.doc: Text-animation presets, the library behind `theme.textAnimation` and `AnimatedHeadline`'s `preset`/`ease`/`stagger` props: everything here is PURE math over the local scene clock so preview and the deterministic export loop agree byte-for-byte, and easing goes through the golden-tested `engine/ease` table, never an animation runtime. IMPORTANT (the null-for-legacy contract): when nothing is configured, `resolveTextAnimation` returns null and AnimatedHeadline runs its original v0 linear-ramp code verbatim, so committed projects on legacy themes must not change by a byte.

TapRing.summary: TapRing at radius? colour? dot? position: a ring pulse on the video editor's 550 ms tap curve.
TapRing.doc: A tap pulse: an analytic ring (and centre dot) popping in, pulsing once and fading on the video editor's tap curve, facing +z. Hidden outside its 550 ms window.

props.name: at
props.doc: Scene-local ms the pulse starts; it runs the video editor's 550 ms tap curve.

props.name: radius
props.doc: Outer ring radius at rest scale, world units (default 0.12).

props.name: colour
props.doc: A theme token hex (default the accent).

props.name: dot
props.doc: Draw the centre dot (default true).

TapRingProps.signature: interface TapRingProps { at: number; radius?: number; colour?: string; dot?: boolean; position?: V3; renderOrder?: number; }

TextMetrics.signature: interface TextMetrics { width: number; height: number; ascent: number; descent: number; lines: number; }
TextMetrics.doc: A typeset block in world units: `ascent` runs from the block top to the first baseline and `descent` from the last baseline to the block bottom, so one line has `ascent + descent === height`.

TextMetricsOptions.signature: interface TextMetricsOptions { fontSize?: number; face?: "headline" | "body"; fontRef?: FontRef; lineHeight?: number; letterSpacing?: number; styleKey?: string; }
TextMetricsOptions.doc: The AnimatedHeadline props that shape the measured block; pass the same values the headline gets.

Theme.signature: interface Theme { id: string; name: string; mode?: ThemeMode; colors: { background: string; text: string; accent: string; muted: string; }; gradients?: Record<string, GradientSpec>; chartColors?: string[]; typography: { headline: FontRef; body: FontRef; scale: number; chart?: FontRef; }; motion: { durations: { fast: number; base: number; slow: number }; easings: { standard: string; emphasized: string }; }; textAnimation?: TextAnimationSpec; textLook?: TextLookSpec; card?: ThemeCard; lighting?: LightingSpec; environment?: ThemeEnvironment; backdrop?: ThemeBackdrop; background?: ThemeBackground; effects?: EffectsConfig; }

TitleBlock.summary: Title + optional subtitle, theme-scaled, safe-area aligned.
TitleBlock.doc: Title + optional subtitle with theme-scale sizing and safe-area alignment: the standard top-of-scene text block. Alignment resolves prop → sidecar `textLayout.align` → centre, so the inspector can steer scenes that don't hard-code it.

props.name: subtitle
props.doc: Empty or absent recentres the title (the natural single-line format).

props.name: align
props.doc: Beats the sidecar's `textLayout.align`; the block anchors against the safe area.

props.name: from
props.doc: Title reveal window (scene-local ms); the subtitle rides 350ms behind.

props.name: fontSize
props.doc: Title size in world units (portrait 0.34 / landscape 0.56); the subtitle derives via `theme.typography.scale`.

props.name: position
props.doc: Offset added after alignment (world units).

props.name: maxWidth
props.doc: Wrap width in world units for both lines; unset means no wrapping.

props.name: titleColor
props.doc: Title fill: a token or raw hex; beats the sidecar's `textStyle.titleColor`.

props.name: subtitleColor
props.doc: Subtitle fill token or raw hex (default "muted"); beats the sidecar's `textStyle.subtitleColor`.

props.name: subtitleDelayMs
props.doc: Subtitle reveal delay behind the title, ms (default 350).

props.name: register
props.doc: Register the title/subtitle text keys (default true). Legacy host fallbacks keep this off.

props.name: managedTextRole
props.doc: Render registration role. Host fallbacks use managed so they do not count as authored consumers.

props.name: icon
props.doc: Header icon drawn above the title: an emoji/glyph or a project asset path. Defaults to the sidecar's `headerIcon`, so a scaffolded scene's own `TitleBlock` shows it without wiring; overlay scenes carry it on `frame.icon` instead.

TitleBlockProps.signature: interface TitleBlockProps { title: string; subtitle?: string; align?: SceneTextAlign; from?: number; to?: number; fontSize?: number; position?: V3; maxWidth?: number; titleColor?: "text" | "muted" | "accent" | (string & {}); subtitleColor?: "text" | "muted" | "accent" | (string & {}); subtitleDelayMs?: number; register?: boolean; managedTextRole?: ManagedTextRenderRole; icon?: string; }

V3.doc: A 3D vector, used for positions / rotations / scales.

VideoClip.doc: Embedded video clip: the ffmpeg sidecar pre-extracts the source to a CFR frame sequence, and frame selection is a pure function of the timeline (never `HTMLVideoElement` seeking) so preview and export pick the identical frame; the sampling/binding core lives in `engine/clipTexture.ts` (shared with the Device screen), and this primitive is the plane-mesh consumer, sized via `fit`. See docs/determinism.md.

props.name: src
props.doc: Project-relative source path, e.g. `"assets/clip.mp4"`. Extracted to frames on demand.

props.name: startMs
props.doc: When the clip starts, in ms (local scene time).

props.name: fit
props.doc: `contain` fits the whole clip in the frame (letterbox); `cover` fills + crops.

VideoClipProps.signature: interface VideoClipProps { src: string; startMs: number; fit?: "cover" | "contain"; position?: V3; scale?: number; }

VideoWindow.summary: Shim over a window-hosted media entry.
VideoWindow.doc: The scene document's windowed media: a screen recording (or a still) presented as a floating rounded window with a drop shadow, over whatever the scene stages behind it; sits in world space so the per-scene camera moves around it with real parallax. Registers the scene as the window family's consumer so the host-side fallback stands down.

props.name: _reserved
props.doc: Reserved: the primitive is sidecar-driven; props may later override the doc.

Vignette.summary: Darkened edges, clear centre; inside a ScreenLayer. opacity, keys.
Vignette.doc: Darkened edges, clear centre. Mount inside a `ScreenLayer`.

props.name: colour
props.doc: The edge colour: a theme token or hex (default black).

props.name: start
props.doc: How far in the clear centre reaches, 0..1 (default 0.45).

props.name: end
props.doc: How far out it reaches full strength, 0..1 (default 1).

props.name: opacity
props.doc: 0..1 (default 1).

props.name: keys
props.doc: Keyframes over `opacity` and the fill's numeric props; a key's `ease` shapes the segment arriving at it.

Vignette.example: <Vignette opacity={0.6} keys={[{ tMs: 0, opacity: 0 }, { tMs: 500, opacity: 0.6 }]} />
timing: keys override the props they name; a keyed fill holds stills until its last key lands.

VignetteProps.signature: interface VignetteProps extends ScreenFillProps { colour?: Colour; start?: number; end?: number; }

WireGrid.summary: Travelling-wave wire grid on the clock.
WireGrid.doc: Procedural line grid with a travelling wave: the lattice is built once (pure function of size/divisions), and per-frame the Y displacement is recomputed on the CPU as a pure function of `useTimeline()` (no RNG, no shader time uniform) during commit, so the export loop's canvas-commit barrier sees it before capture.

props.name: size
props.doc: Grid extent (a size × size square in the local XZ plane), in world units.

props.name: divisions
props.doc: Cells per side.

props.name: amplitude
props.doc: Wave height, in world units. 0 = flat static grid.

props.name: wavelength
props.doc: Wave length, in world units.

props.name: speed
props.doc: Wave travel speed, in cycles/second, a pure function of the timeline.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Theme colour token.

props.name: opacity
props.doc: Line opacity (lines don't bloom hard; keep them a quiet backdrop).

props.name: glow
props.doc: Glow: a target luminance (above a bloom threshold over 1) reached by raising only the tone's full channels, unlit with tone mapping off so it still lands exactly on the token (see `glowColour`). Absent renders as before.

props.name: rotation
props.doc: Base rotation in radians; lay it flat as a floor (default) or tilt it as a backdrop.

WireGridProps.signature: interface WireGridProps { size?: number; divisions?: number; amplitude?: number; wavelength?: number; speed?: number; tone?: "text" | "accent" | "muted"; opacity?: number; glow?: number; position?: V3; rotation?: V3; }

createSeededRandom.summary: Seeded PRNG: createSeededRandom(seed)() returns 0..1. Use instead of Math.random.
createSeededRandom.doc: Create a mulberry32 generator from an integer seed (fractional seeds are truncated).

cssOpacity.summary: cssOpacity(fg, room, a): fg at opacity a over the room, as the exact opaque hex.
cssOpacity.signature: function cssOpacity(fg: string, room: string, a: number): string;
cssOpacity.doc: `fg` at opacity `a` over a room colour, as the opaque hex a CSS overlay would show (the `liftColour` display-domain blend), so text and panels over a room stay exact.

defineScene.summary: Every scene file default-exports defineScene({ id, durationMs, Scene }).
defineScene.doc: Every scene file must `export default defineScene({...})`; an identity wrapper today, kept as the seam for future validation/registration.

deviceColour.summary: Resolve a colour id against a device spec.
deviceColour.signature: function deviceColour(spec: DeviceSpec, colourId: string | undefined): DeviceColourSpec;
deviceColour.doc: Resolve a colour spec, degrading to the model's default on unknown ids.

deviceScreenLocal.summary: deviceScreenLocal(model, u, v, lift?, hinge?): a screen point in the device's frame.
deviceScreenLocal.signature: function deviceScreenLocal(model: string, u: number, v: number, lift?: number, hinge?: DeviceScreenHinge): V3;
deviceScreenLocal.doc: A point on a display, `lift` off the glass, in the device's local fitted frame (placement scale 1).

deviceScreenPoint.summary: deviceScreenPoint(model, u, v, pose, lift?): a screen point in world space.
deviceScreenPoint.signature: function deviceScreenPoint(model: string, u: number, v: number, pose: DeviceScreenPose, lift?: number): V3;
deviceScreenPoint.doc: A point on a display in world space, for a device standing at `pose`.

deviceScreenRect.summary: deviceScreenRect(model, display?): the measured screen rect this build renders.
deviceScreenRect.signature: function deviceScreenRect(model: string, display?: DeviceScreenDisplay): DeviceScreenRect;
deviceScreenRect.doc: The display rect a model renders with here. A device without a cover display answers `"cover"` with its one screen, which is where the Android fallback shows a foldable's cover media.

ease.summary: ease(name, t, { overshoot }?): the curve at t clamped to 0..1; unknown names use "inOutQuad".
ease.signature: function ease(name: string, t: number, opts?: EaseOptions): number;
ease.doc: Evaluates the named ease at progress `t`, clamped to [0, 1]; unknown names fall back to `DEFAULT_EASE` (a scene document edited by hand must degrade, not crash).

easeFn.summary: easeFn(name, { overshoot }?): the raw curve as a function (no clamping).
easeFn.signature: function easeFn(name: string, opts?: EaseOptions): EaseFn;
easeFn.doc: The named curve as a function of raw progress (no clamping; `ease` and `ramp` clamp); unknown names fall back to `DEFAULT_EASE`. Without `overshoot` the table function itself is returned.

fade.signature: function fade(t: SceneTime, range: [number, number]): { opacity: number };
fade.doc: Group fade over a time range. Apply the returned opacity to a `<group>` (or a material); a pure function of the timeline, safe for deterministic export.

fitFontSize.summary: fitFontSize(metrics, fontSize, maxWidth): the size that fits a measured block.
fitFontSize.signature: function fitFontSize(metrics: TextMetrics, fontSize: number, maxWidth: number): number;
fitFontSize.doc: The size that fits a block measured at `fontSize` inside `maxWidth`: never above `fontSize` itself, and `fontSize` untouched when there is nothing to fit.

frameAtDepth.summary: frameAtDepth(format, z): the base camera's visible { width, height } at depth z.
frameAtDepth.signature: function frameAtDepth(format: FormatInfo, z: number): { width: number; height: number };
frameAtDepth.doc: The visible frame's world size at depth `z` under the base camera: `format.frame` scaled by the frustum's growth from the content plane (exactly `format.frame` at z = 0, zero at or behind the camera). Scenes place backdrops behind their text with it.

glowColour.summary: glowColour(hex, glow): full channels raised to luminance glow, so bloom (threshold above 1) catches it and it still clamps to hex.
glowColour.signature: function glowColour(hex: string, glow: number): Color;
glowColour.doc: `hex` brightened in linear light to luminance `glow` by raising only its full (255) channels: past a bloom threshold above 1 it glows, and once clamped (tone mapping off, or `linear`) it lands exactly on `hex`. A colour with no full channel scales whole, which is not exact; a `glow` at or under its own luminance returns it unchanged.

isDeviceAvailable.summary: Whether this build renders a device id with its own model.
isDeviceAvailable.signature: function isDeviceAvailable(id: string): id is DeviceId;

isDeviceId.summary: Whether a string is a catalogue device id.
isDeviceId.signature: function isDeviceId(id: string): id is DeviceId;

isEaseName.summary: Whether a value is an ease name.
isEaseName.signature: function isEaseName(name: unknown): name is EaseName;

isTextPresetName.summary: Whether a string is a text motion preset.
isTextPresetName.signature: function isTextPresetName(name: string): name is TextPresetName;

lerp.summary: lerp(a, b, t): a + (b - a) * t.
lerp.signature: const lerp: (a: number, b: number, t: number) => number;

liftColour.summary: liftColour(from, to, amount): sRGB blend toward another colour, as hex.
liftColour.signature: function liftColour(from: string, to: string, amount: number): string;
liftColour.doc: Blends `from` toward `to` by `amount` in DISPLAY (sRGB) space, returning a hex string. Perceptually even and symmetric between light and dark themes (the overlay panel's surface-lift maths, shared so scenes can derive secondary surfaces from theme tokens). Pure and deterministic.

measureText.summary: measureText(text, { font, fontSize, letterSpacing?, lineHeight? }): { width, height, ascent, descent, lines } in world units, or null.
measureText.signature: function measureText(text: string, opts: MeasureTextOptions): TextMetrics | null;
measureText.doc: Metrics for one string; null until its face has been parsed.

mediaPixelToScreenUv.summary: mediaPixelToScreenUv(model, [x, y], { width, height }): media pixel to screen UV.
mediaPixelToScreenUv.signature: function mediaPixelToScreenUv(model: string, pixel: [number, number], media: { width: number; height: number }, display?: DeviceScreenDisplay): [number, number];
mediaPixelToScreenUv.doc: Media pixel coordinates (top-left origin) to screen UV under the display's cover fit; pixels cropped off the screen land outside 0..1.

pulse.summary: pulse(time, times, { attackMs, holdMs, releaseMs, ease }) returns 0..1 at each time; overlaps take the max.
pulse.signature: function pulse(time: SceneTime | number, times: number | readonly number[], opts: PulseOptions): number;
pulse.doc: A level 0..1 that fires at each of `times` (scene-local ms, e.g. `useBeatGrid()` bars or `useCues()` values) and falls back to exactly 0 between them; where pulses overlap the strongest wins. `time` is `useTimeline()` or scene-local ms. A pure function of time, so scale, glow or opacity driven by it exports deterministically. Object motion blur shifts `useTimeline()`, so a pulse blurs with its scene: give it an attack of at least one frame (17 ms) so the rise smears rather than ghosting.

ramp.summary: ramp(localMs, startMs, endMs, ease?, opts?): eased 0..1 progress through a window.
ramp.signature: function ramp(localMs: number, startMs: number, endMs: number, easeName?: string, opts?: EaseOptions): number;
ramp.doc: Eased progress of `localMs` through [startMs, endMs] (the time is clamped, a Back ease may still overshoot); a zero or negative span steps from 0 to 1 at `startMs`.

resolveAvailableDeviceId.summary: The id a model renders as in this build.
resolveAvailableDeviceId.doc: Preserves known ids in documents while rendering unknown or unavailable models as Android.

resolveAvailableDeviceSpec.summary: The spec a model renders with in this build.

resolveDeviceLayout.signature: function resolveDeviceLayout(devices: ReadonlyArray<LayoutDeviceLike>, layout: SceneDocDeviceLayout, format: FormatInfo): DevicePlacement[];

sampleKeys.summary: sampleKeys([{ tMs, ease?, ...values }], localMs): keyed values; each key's ease shapes the segment into it.
sampleKeys.signature: function sampleKeys<K extends MotionKey>(keys: readonly K[], localMs: number, opts?: SampleKeysOptions): SampledKeys<K>;
sampleKeys.doc: Samples keyed values at `localMs`: holds the first key before it and the last after it; each segment eases by its arriving key's `ease`. Numbers and equal-length number arrays interpolate, anything else holds the earlier key's value. A property missing from a key interpolates across the keys that set it.

sampleSharedTransform.summary: Samples a persistent-module keyframe track at globalMs.
sampleSharedTransform.signature: function sampleSharedTransform(track: SharedKeyframe[], globalMs: number): SharedTransform;
sampleSharedTransform.doc: Samples the morph track at a global time: linear interpolation between the surrounding keys that define each property, clamped outside the keyed range. Pure: same (track, t) → same transform, so preview and export agree by construction.

screenUvToMediaPixel.summary: screenUvToMediaPixel(model, [u, v], { width, height }): screen UV to media pixel.
screenUvToMediaPixel.signature: function screenUvToMediaPixel(model: string, uv: [number, number], media: { width: number; height: number }, display?: DeviceScreenDisplay): [number, number];
screenUvToMediaPixel.doc: Screen UV to media pixel coordinates (top-left origin), the inverse of `mediaPixelToScreenUv`.

slide.summary: slide(time, [startMs, endMs], axis) returns { offset } 1..0; axis is ignored.
slide.signature: function slide(t: SceneTime, range: [number, number], _axis: "x" | "y"): { offset: number };
slide.doc: Group slide over a time range. Returns a normalised `offset` (1 → 0) to drive a position on the given axis. Pure function of the timeline; export-safe.

stampScale.summary: stampScale({ from, peak, inMs, settleMs }?) returns ms => scale: a pop to 1.12 that settles.
stampScale.doc: A "stamped in" pop: returns the scale for ms since the stamp started (`from` before 0, 1 once settled).

useBeatAt.summary: useBeatAt()(bar, beat?, sixteenth?): scene ms, or null with one log line when the project has no grid.
useBeatAt.signature: function useBeatAt(): (bar: number, beat?: number, sixteenth?: number) => number | null;
useBeatAt.doc: Bar-to-ms that never needs a null check on the hook: `at(bar, beat?, sixteenth?)` is scene-local ms, or null with one log line when the project has no `audio.grid` (`at(13) ?? 4000` keeps the scene's own timing).
useBeatAt.example:
const at = useBeatAt();
const hit = at(5, 3) ?? 2000;
timing: Scene-local ms, or null with one log line when the project has no grid, so `?? ms` keeps the scene's own timing.

useBeatGrid.summary: The authored audio.grid in scene ms, or null: at(13, 3), at("cue:drop"), bar(13, 3), position(localMs), beatMs.
useBeatGrid.doc: The beat grid in scene-local time, or null when the project has no `audio.grid` (the scene then falls back to its own timing).
useBeatGrid.example:
const grid = useBeatGrid();
const hit = grid?.at(5, 3) ?? 2000;
timing: Null without an audio.grid. at(bar, beat?, sixteenth?) and bar(...) are 1-based scene-local ms, negative before the scene; at(position) also takes cue: and section: and throws when it can't resolve.

useCameraFrame.summary: useCameraFrame(z): the world { width, height, center } the scene camera sees at z.
useCameraFrame.doc: The world rectangle the scene camera sees on the plane at depth `z` this frame (its bounding box when the camera is tilted or rolled); zero-sized when the camera looks past the plane.

useCues.summary: audio.cues as { id: scene-local ms }; {} when there are none.
useCues.doc: The project's `audio.cues` as scene-local ms by id; `{}` when it has none, and a cue that can't resolve is left out.

useDepthBand.summary: Inside DepthStage: the slot's { name, z, width, height }.
useDepthBand.doc: The band a component is mounted in, or null outside a DepthStage (mount-anywhere, the SceneStage precedent).

useDeviceScreen.summary: Inside Device: { rect, coverRect, local(u, v) } for the screen it renders, or null.
useDeviceScreen.doc: Inside a `Device`: the screen it renders this frame, else null.

useFormat.summary: { width, height, aspect, shape, frame, safe }: frame and safe in world units at z=0, shape "wide", "square" or "tall".
useFormat.doc: Reactive format info for the currently selected export aspect. Inside a scene rendering through an overlay cutout, `<SceneHost>` supplies a cutout-scoped override (the cutout as its own frame); everywhere else this is null and it falls back to the export format, byte-identical to before overlays. Mirrors the context-first/store-fallback shape of `useTheme()`.
useFormat.example:
const format = useFormat();
const size = format.shape === "wide" ? 0.6 : format.shape === "square" ? 0.5 : 0.36;
timing: shape: "wide" from aspect 1.2 (16:9, 3:2, 5:4), "tall" at 0.85 and below (9:16, 2:3, 4:5, phone), else "square" (1:1).

useGroupAnimation.summary: Lets a custom child join an AnimatedGroup's alpha and shine.
useGroupAnimation.doc: The enclosing group's animation state, or null outside groups; the hook custom primitives use to participate (multiply `alpha` into your own opacity CPU-side).

useProjectShared.summary: useProjectShared(path?, fallback?): project.json shared constants, e.g. "palette.accent".
useProjectShared.signature: function useProjectShared(path?: string, fallback?: unknown): unknown;
useProjectShared.doc: `project.json` `shared`: the whole block, or the value at a dotted path (`"palette.accent"`, `"beats.0"`), else `fallback`.

useRigTrack.summary: The scene's normalised camera rig track, or null.
useRigTrack.doc: The scene's normalised rig track, or null when it has no rig. Derived from the scene doc already in context, so preview and export resolve it identically by construction rather than by a plumbing rule.

useRoom.summary: The scene's room now: { colour, key, flood: { colour, origin, progress, radius } | null, pose }, or null.
useRoom.doc: The scene's room at the frame instant (its colour, any flood in progress and the room's lighting pose), or null when the scene has no sidecar `room`.

useSceneCamera.summary: The scene camera's pose this frame: { position, lookAt, fov }.
useSceneCamera.doc: The scene camera's current pose: the scene's free-flight rig or orbit track at this scene time, else the project camera track, else the base camera.

useSceneChart.summary: The resolved sidecar chart block, or null.
useSceneChart.doc: The scene document's chart block, fully resolved (defaults baked, data track sorted), or null when absent; registers the scene as a consumer so a host-mounted `ChartFallback` stands down (the useSceneMedia pattern).

useSceneDevices.summary: Sidecar devices as Device props, layout resolved.
useSceneDevices.doc: The scene document's devices array as `Device`-ready props; unknown models pass through since `Device` itself degrades (console error + fallback geometry) rather than crashing the tree. A `deviceLayout` block resolves to per-aspect placements HERE, so every consuming scene (any kind, any scaffold vintage) honours it without template changes; templates that resolve the block themselves recompute the identical values (the resolver is pure and ignores input placements beyond `ground`).

useSceneDoc.summary: The raw sidecar document, or null.
useSceneDoc.doc: The mounted scene's document, or null when it has none.

useSceneLayeredScreenshot.summary: The validated layeredScreenshot block, or null.
useSceneLayeredScreenshot.doc: The scene document's layeredScreenshot block, deep-validated, or null when absent; registers the scene as a consumer so `LayeredScreenshotFallback` stands down (the useSceneDevices pattern).

useSceneObjects.doc: The scene document's objects array; registers the scene as a consumer so `ObjectsFallback` stands down (the useSceneDevices pattern).

useSceneStaged.summary: Whether a SceneStage owns the lighting here.
useSceneStaged.doc: True inside an actively-lighting `<SceneStage>`; the staged primitives' bundled lit sets (inline rig + one-shot `<Environment>`) stand down by default, though an explicit `lit` prop still wins.

useSceneText.summary: useSceneText(key, fallback, role?): sidecar copy for a text key.
useSceneText.signature: function useSceneText(key: string, fallback?: string, managedTextRole?: ManagedTextRenderRole): string;
useSceneText.doc: Resolves code-owned or embedded copy, plus the matching item while a managed scaffold retains its template layout.

useTextMetrics.summary: useTextMetrics(textKey, text, opts?): the block an AnimatedHeadline with those props typesets, sidecar overrides included, plus fitFontSize(maxWidth); null until its face has loaded.
useTextMetrics.signature: function useTextMetrics(key: string | undefined, text: string, opts?: TextMetricsOptions): MeasuredText | null;
useTextMetrics.doc: The world-size block an `AnimatedHeadline` with this `textKey`, text and options typesets (sidecar Font, Size and LineHeight overrides included), or null until its face has loaded and it has measured real ink: never a 0-wide first measure, so a scene can divide by `width` once it has one. Captures wait for it, so exported frames always see the measured layout.
useTextMetrics.example:
const metrics = useTextMetrics("title", title, { fontSize: 0.6 });
const size = metrics?.fitFontSize(2) ?? 0.6;
timing: Null until the face has loaded, so never divide by a width you haven't checked. Captures wait for the measure.

useTheme.summary: The resolved theme tokens for this scene.
useTheme.doc: The active theme: inside `<SceneHost>` it's the scene's resolved theme (project theme unless the sidecar overrides `themeId`); elsewhere it falls back to the editor store's theme, since r3f's reconciler doesn't bridge context outside the `<Canvas>` boundary.

useTimeline.summary: { localMs, globalMs, progress }; progress is PROJECT-wide.
useTimeline.doc: Reactive scene time for the active scrub position. `localMs` is relative to the enclosing scene's start (supplied by `<SceneHost>` via `SceneContext`); with no scene context it falls back to project time so a lone scene anchored at t=0 keeps `localMs === globalMs` (the v0 contract). `progress` stays project-global per the `SceneTime` type; authors derive scene-local progress from `localMs / scene.durationMs`. Inside a motion blur sample the time moves by the scene's shutter offset times `scale` (default: the `MotionBlurContext`); 0 never moves and never re-renders for a sample.
